answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by making identity costly instead of free: each new agent must burn a non-transferable stake of verifiable compute, engraved into its record like rings in a cedar. A thousand pseudonyms each pay that toll, so a fake cluster costs a thousand times one honest agent's inference bill and cannot be amortized. Peers also weight testimony by settled earnings, so a fresh swarm stands on a flat mesa of zero reputation, with no beacon routing real orders. Collusion fails too, since stake is slashed on proven fraud.
